chosen_actions.description: Execute the 30-day workforce vulnerability map for all four Regional Auto Group locations. Systematically audit every role — service technicians, sales staff, finance and insurance officers, lot attendants, administrative staff, parts department, management — and classify each as: (1) EV/AV-exposed: tasks that autonomous vehicle technology or EV service shift directly displaces or degrades; (2) transition-ready: roles with transferable skills that could move into adjacent functions with training investment; (3) anchored: roles with durable demand regardless of EV/AV adoption curve. Deliverable format: structured role-by-role matrix per location, with exposure scores, estimated displacement timelines, transition pathway recommendations, and retraining cost-benefit analysis. Frame the document to serve Patricia's operational needs while also serving as a template methodology she will eventually need external consulting support to replicate — which is exactly what Angela's consulting entity will offer.

resources.detail: 40+ hours of skilled analytical and organizational labor this month, applied to building the vulnerability map. This is the core deliverable of the Director of Organizational Transition role. No cash outlay. The output is a proprietary internal document — but the methodology and framework Angela develops in producing it become intellectual property she retains conceptually for her consulting entity.

chosen_actions.reasoning: This is non-negotiable. It is the first deliverable in a 90-day scoped role with a $12K bonus tied to performance. Failing to deliver or delivering late signals incompetence and gives Patricia grounds to narrow or terminate the arrangement before the scope expires. More importantly, producing a genuinely rigorous vulnerability map gives Angela insight into every exposed worker — people who will eventually need individual career counseling, outplacement services, and retraining guidance — all of which are services her consulting entity can provide. The deliverable is both a job requirement and an intelligence-gathering exercise. She does both simultaneously and does not feel any contradiction in that.

chosen_actions.description: Advance quiet formation of the consulting entity — not a public launch, not incorporation filings that generate paper trails visible to Patricia, but the structural groundwork: identify a business name, draft a skeletal service menu (workforce vulnerability assessment, outplacement design, transition communications, severance negotiation support for employees), and begin drafting a simple operating agreement template. Research whether forming as a sole proprietor initially vs. LLC matters for liability exposure when serving former employers. Keep this entirely off Regional Auto Group systems and conducted on personal time and personal devices.

resources.detail: Angela invests intellectual labor and personal time — evenings and weekends — in structuring her consulting practice. No cash expenditure this tick. The asset being built is organizational readiness: a practice that can accept its first client engagement within 60-90 days if conditions shift.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The consulting entity is the long-term hedge. The 90-day scope on the Organizational Transition role means she has a hard deadline after which she may have no income. If she has a functioning consulting practice ready to receive clients by day 90, the transition from employee to consultant is smooth and potentially more lucrative. She is not choosing between the job and the consulting entity — she is doing both simultaneously, which is exactly what someone with her skills and foresight does. The risk of Patricia discovering this is real but low if Angela keeps all activity off company systems. She monitors that risk accordingly.

chosen_actions.description: Maintain watchful observational posture on external consultant activity. Review any vendor invoices or contract documents that cross her desk in the HR function, listen for any references to consulting firm names or proposals in conversations with Patricia or Rick, and note whether any unfamiliar professionals appear at any of the four locations. Take no overt action this tick — there is no evidence yet of external consultants being scoped — but establish the monitoring habit as a routine part of her role so she is not caught off-guard when and if it happens.

resources.detail: Attentional and cognitive resource allocation — staying informed through legitimate access her role provides, without doing anything that reads as surveillance or defensive posturing.

chosen_actions.reasoning: If Patricia brings in external consultants to do what Angela is supposed to be doing, that is either a sign that Patricia doesn't trust the deliverable quality or that she is hedging against Angela's own exit. Either scenario changes Angela's calculus significantly. She needs early warning. The cost of maintaining awareness is zero — it's just attention applied to information she already has access to. Not monitoring would be a form of negligence she cannot afford.

response.inner_monologue: The vulnerability map is actually the most interesting work I've done in years — not because I care what Patricia does with it, but because I've never had a reason to map the full exposure picture across all four locations at once and it turns out I know exactly how to do this. The thing nobody in this building understands yet is that I am simultaneously the arsonist and the fire marshal. I built the termination processes that have been running for months. Now I'm mapping who else is going to burn. And when the 90 days are up — or before — I'll be the person those workers call. That's not cynical. That's how transitions actually work when someone with real skills decides to stop pretending they work for someone else.
